source_caption:
One of Tobey Maguire’s most intense performances ever.

For Brothers (2009), Maguire played Sam Cahill, a Marine who is captured while serving in Afghanistan and returns home deeply traumatized by what he experienced.

To make the transformation feel real, Maguire lost more than 20 pounds for the role, going from around 158 pounds to about 136 at his lowest. He said he spent roughly four and a half weeks dieting and training for the weight loss, and admitted it was difficult and not something he would recommend.

But the physical transformation was only part of it.

Maguire later said he lost much of his joy while making the film. He described the experience as so emotionally draining that he didn’t realize how much it had affected him until near the end of filming, when he suddenly started joking and laughing again and felt an enormous sense of release.

That intensity comes through in the movie, especially during Sam’s breakdown after returning home from captivity. His character is dealing with trauma, guilt, anger and the feeling that his family has moved on without him.

It’s a completely different side of Maguire from the Spider-Man movies.

And it’s one of those performances that makes you forget you’re watching an actor.

You’re just watching a man completely fall apart.
